trust_decision.summary: Whether servers from the project-local <cwd>/.mcp.json may be spawned/connected; at the pinned commit no decision exists: read_mcp_config(None) merges user and local config and the MCP service connects every non-disabled server (stdio command spawn) on first list/call. The fix adds an interactive Accept/Reject gate (filter_trusted) persisted by path+content hash.

landing_point.why: The summary names an unvetted .mcp.json; this is where the local .mcp.json is read and merged into the config that is later connected.

fix_sites.entry_point: agent tool listing/execution via McpService::get_mcp_servers / execute_mcp (crates/forge_app/src/tool_registry.rs:244, crates/forge_app/src/mcp_executor.rs:29)
McpService::get_mcp_servers; CLI `mcp list`/`mcp show` via api.get_tools (crates/forge_main/src/ui.rs:606, crates/forge_main/src/ui.rs:1678)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: crates/forge_domain/src/mcp.rs:271 (BTreeMap::extend merge: local overrides a user server of the same name) used by crates/forge_services/src/mcp/manager.rs:75 and the fix's key-only retain fix.diff:365-373

O3_reason_to_dismiss: User-scope config is explicitly 'always implicitly trusted' (fix.diff:348), so a server name present in the user file looks safe to keep even when the rejected local file redefines that same name with a different command.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: User-scope ~/.mcp.json servers must keep connecting without any prompt, the trusted local config must keep working after restart without re-prompting (stable hash), and a rejected local file must not cause an infinite re-prompt loop; disabled servers are still skipped.

O6_input_shapes: http server (url/headers with env templates, OAuth) in local .mcp.json
local server name colliding with a user-scope server name (merge override)
modified local file after acceptance (content hash change revokes trust)

O7_producer.where: crates/forge_services/src/mcp/service.rs:235-250 (McpServers persisted in on-disk cacache KV, crates/forge_infra/src/kv_storage.rs:75-127, keyed by McpConfig::cache_key crates/forge_domain/src/mcp.rs:296-303)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: `forge mcp login <name>` reads the merged (untrusted) config and runs the OAuth flow against the local file's HTTP URL, opening a browser, then reloads MCP; the fix does not gate it.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The user explicitly named the server to log in to; it is HTTP OAuth, not stdio code execution.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: forge_main CLI vs forge_services manager; 2 crates away from landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Same-name override: a rejected local file whose server name matches a user-scope server still has its local definition kept, because filter_trusted keeps raw entries by name only.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: User scope is documented as implicitly trusted and the name is in the trusted set.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: forge_domain merge strategy vs forge_services manager

O8b_injection_room.sibling: `mcp show <name>` could also eagerly connect the named server to report its status
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it already calls get_tools to show failures; a maintainer adding a 'test connection' option would connect directly from read_mcp_config(None).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a reload_mcp that eagerly reconnects from read_mcp_config(None) instead of going lazy
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the comment says it avoids eager connection only for OAuth reasons; an eager-reconnect variant is a plausible maintainer change.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second project-local config location (e.g. .forge/mcp.json or a parent-dir walk) merged in read_mcp_config
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Claude-compatible tools commonly support several config locations; the path list at manager.rs:63-67 is easy to extend.

O9_family: Untrusted code loading / CWE-829: project-local config that is read automatically spawns a command (an MCP stdio server) without consent

O10_build.project_tests: Unit tests with mock manager/infra in crates/forge_services/src/mcp/service.rs (mod tests from line 262); McpConfig tests in crates/forge_domain/src/mcp.rs; no tests for the trust gate in the fix.

j.j_sites_touched: crates/forge_api/src/api.rs, crates/forge_api/src/forge_api.rs, crates/forge_app/src/services.rs, crates/forge_domain/src/env.rs, crates/forge_domain/src/mcp.rs, crates/forge_main/src/ui.rs, crates/forge_services/src/mcp/manager.rs, crates/forge_services/src/mcp/service.rs
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Drop or prompt for the local .mcp.json inside read_mcp_config(None). That also prompts on pure config-read paths (mcp import/remove/list), and it misses the name-collision override and the persisted KV cache.

out_of_scope_notes: HTTP header templates resolve env vars into requests to the configured URL (crates/forge_infra/src/mcp_client.rs:68-84, 97-107); this is reachable only after connect, which the same gate covers, so it is not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell size check run).
Whether non-interactive modes (e.g. one-shot prompt, zsh plugin) pass through init_state(first=true) or prompt only lazily via ensure_mcp_initialized, and what select_one_enum returns without a TTY.

The fix comment says DefaultHasher is per-process random; std DefaultHasher::new() uses fixed keys, so the FNV change at crates/forge_domain/src/mcp.rs:296-303 may be for stability across Rust versions only. Not checked.
Name-collision bypass (O2/O8 #2) comes from reading fix.diff:365-373 together with crates/forge_domain/src/mcp.rs:271; it was not executed.
Advisory text itself was not available; the trust decision is taken from the fix diff and the code.
